first.title: One never-valid record from any member stops another member's result counting under a declaration rule
first.scenario: Goal under `open` (the same holds for `independent-attempts`, the ship tasks of `pipeline`, the shared files of an `open` goal, and any hand-written rule with a declaration part). Member A posts result X and declares it done; X counts. Member M, running a modified daemon, signs one `CompletionDeclared` (a review or a check record works too) that names X, with its `anchor` field set to any id that is not a host record on the chain, for example X's own id. `Header::check` accepts any anchor, `screen` keeps it because M is admitted, and every computer holds it as pending forever. When X is judged without pinned evidence, `predicate` walks every held witness of X. For a declaration rule the 'latest' filter is `_ => Some(candidate.id())`, so no standing test runs before `self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?`. The anchor has no snapshot, `resolve` returns `Pending(Anchor)`, and `?` aborts the whole predicate. `approval(X)` is now an error on every computer. It should skip a witness that is not effective, as the code before this commit did (it only tested `status == Effective` and resolved nothing per witness). A milder honest form: any member's declaration or opinion about X that arrives before the host record it names makes X flip to not counted until that record arrives.
first.evidence: fold.rs:1091-1103 (declaration arm passes every witness to `resolve` before any standing test; the standing test is at 1147). fold.rs:116-119 (`resolve` fails when the anchor has no snapshot). fold.rs:53-58 (witness index holds every held record, whatever its standing). chain.rs:444-447 (unknown anchor is Pending, the record stays held). node/replica.rs:210 (ingest screens by author only). Consequences: projection.rs:209-221 (`.ok().flatten()` gives approved = false, round not completed, so the task can be started again); flow.rs:209-212 (`self.approval(..)?` makes `stage_ready` an error, so a stage that waits on completion is never wanted); node/requests/tasks.rs:300 (a pick copies evidence from state, now empty, and trial replay refuses it as 'cannot be applied yet'); node/requests/workspace.rs:558 (integrate answers 'exact workspace candidate lacks required evidence'). Removing M does not help: the record stays held. Reviews and Check rules are safe because `latest_review` returns only effective records. The pre-commit predicate (git show 8c086c1^) had no per-witness resolve.
first.fix: In `predicate`, test `self.status(candidate.id(), proof) == Standing::Effective` before resolving at the witness's anchor (or `continue` when the anchor has no snapshot). Add a signed replay test: under `open`, a second member's declaration of the same subject signed with an anchor that is not a host record leaves the author's declared result approved, forward, reversed and after a reload; repeat for a stage that requires completion and for a shared-files change.
first.person_sees: In a goal where members say their own work is done, one member with altered software can post a single bad record about someone else's result. That result then shows as not done on every computer, its task shows as free to take again, the lead cannot pick it, a later pipeline step waiting on it never opens, and a file change under the same rule cannot be accepted. Removing the member does not bring the result back; its author has to post it again.

second.statement: In `Verifier::predicate`, a declaration-type rule resolves role holders at every held witness's anchor before testing that the witness is effective, so one held witness whose anchor has no chain snapshot turns `approval(X)` into `Err(Pending(Anchor))` on every computer. Any admitted member can sign such a record about another member's result; this commit introduced it (the per-witness `resolve(..)?` at fold.rs:1103 is new), and it is still present at HEAD 5b3fe29.
second.scenario:
1. Goal under `open` (default completion is `Declaration { by: ContributionAuthor }`, organization.rs:218-223; same for `independent-attempts`, the `ship` tasks of `pipeline`, shared files of such a goal, and any hand-written rule with a Declaration part). A publishes X and declares it; X counts.
2. Member M's modified daemon signs one CompletionDeclared / ReviewRecorded / CheckAttested with `subject = X` and `anchor` = any id that is not a governance record in the host chain (X's id works). `Header::check` only requires the anchor to be present (event.rs:821); `screen` keeps it because M was admitted (screen.rs:23-43); `advance` refuses non-effective events only when locally authored (commit.rs:340-360). `authorize_base` gives it `Pending(Waiting::Anchor)` and it stays held (chain.rs:444-447). It sits at M's log tip, so sync carries it everywhere.
3. `Verifier::new` indexes it as a witness of X regardless of standing (fold.rs:53-58).
4. `project` calls `approval(X, None, None)` (projection.rs:209). In `predicate`, the unpinned 'latest' filter for a Declaration rule is `_ => Some(candidate.id())` (fold.rs:1097), so M's record reaches `self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?` (fold.rs:1103); `chain.snapshot` is None, `resolve` returns `Pending(Anchor)` (fold.rs:116-119) and `?` aborts the whole predicate, whatever the order of witnesses.

Removing M changes nothing: the record stays held and indexed.

first.title: Adding a member makes the host's computer sign an offer for every stage task ever opened, finished ones included
first.scenario: Hand-written formation with a flow whose stage task type starts by offer from the task's creator or from members (`Offered { by: task_creator | members, to: members }`). Ten stage tasks have opened over the goal's life; eight are completed, picked or closed. The host adds one member. `desired_effects` calls `offer_templates(binding, stage, None, head)` for every stage of every effective binding. Recipients are now the members at the head (before this commit they were fixed at the binding), the offer's identity includes the recipient, and nothing tests whether the task is still open. So ten new offers are wanted and the host's computer signs all ten, eight of them for work that is over. The same happens when `role give` makes a member match the stage's recipients. Review requests got exactly this guard in the same function (flow.rs:426-493); offers did not. first.title: rules bind refuses a formation that only lists a role without using it, and the refusal does not say which role
first.scenario: A goal is created with --formation independent-attempts, so `lead` has a list (the host's agent) and is a deciding role. On the formations page the host starts from the Independent attempts card and sets "Is one result picked?" to Nobody. The role stays in the Roles list (setPick never removes a role; RoleSettings shows "Not used by any rule.") and the page lights the Open card. The host runs `rules bind --formation-json` with that file and confirms the plan. The daemon answers conflict. It should bind: the new rules give `lead` no kind, replay accepts the binding, and the list is untouched. The reverse also fails: a role added with the editor's "+ Role" button and never wired, then later made the picker, is refused as "a group in this goal" although no rule ever used it and only the host's agent holds it.
first.evidence: goals.rs:162-175 loops over every role the new formation declares that has a list and compares `deciding.contains(role)` with `is_authority_role(&formation, role)`. organization/roles.rs:21-25 answers only whether the role is in `references.authorities`, so a declared role that no rule names reads as a group. chain.rs validate_binding (522-580) checks only roles used as authorities, so replay would accept the binding. The message at goals.rs:170 is "this role picks or closes in this goal and has one holder; these rules make it a group. Use another role name." The role name is only in `details` (goals.rs:174), and the CLI's human output prints `code: message` alone (failure.rs Display, cli/mod.rs print_failure), so the person is not told which role. The plan's message names ROLE, and its exit criterion covers a formation that names `lead` "only in a selector", not one that names it nowhere. node/tests/roles.rs:213 covers only real kind changes and reads no message.
first.fix: Change the code, and have the plan say "names" instead of "declares". In rules_bind, compare kinds only for roles the new formation names in a rule (validation::references(&formation).roles). Count a role as a group only when some held binding names it in a selector and none as an authority. Where a never-used role becomes deciding, require its list to hold exactly one member. Have the CLI print the role from `details` through `safe`. Add both scenarios to rules_bind_is_refused_when_a_role_would_change_kind.
first.person_sees: The host changes the rules on the website so that nobody picks a result, says yes to the plan, and is refused with "this role picks or closes in this goal ... these rules make it a group. Use another role name." The new rules do not use that role at all and the message does not name it. The host has to guess that deleting the unused role from the list makes the change go through.

second.statement: `rules bind` wrongly refuses new rules that still declare a previously deciding role (such as `lead`) but name it in no rule, with a message that says the rules "make it a group" and never says which role. first.title: A held review or declaration whose anchor is not held makes a result stop counting under a declaration rule
first.scenario: Goal under `open` or `independent-attempts` (completion is `Declaration { by: ContributionAuthor }`), or any formation with a Declaration part. Member A posts result X and declares it done; X counts everywhere. Member B sends one review, declaration or check of X whose anchor names an id no computer holds as a host record. A modified daemon can pick any id. An honest daemon's record has the same effect for as long as it is landed before the host record it names (replica.rs:189-216 lands each received batch as it comes and screens by author only). On the next replay X no longer counts. With a made-up anchor it never counts again, and removing B does not help because the record stays held. Expected: a record that is not effective is ignored, as before this commit.
first.evidence: `Verifier::new` indexes every held witness by subject with no standing test (fold.rs:53-58). In `predicate` with no pinned evidence, a Declaration rule takes the `_ => Some(candidate.id())` arm (fold.rs:1091-1101), so every indexed witness reaches fold.rs:1103 `self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?`. `resolve` returns `Err(Pending(Waiting::Anchor))` when the chain has no snapshot for that anchor (fold.rs:116-119), and the `?` ends the whole predicate. projection.rs:209 and :236 turn the error into not approved (`.ok().flatten()`), so `approved` and `round.completed` go false; flow.rs:210 propagates it into `stage_ready`. The `status == Effective` test that used to skip such a witness now comes after the resolve (fold.rs:1147). Reviews and Check rules escape only because `latest_review` filters to effective records first. Before 8c086c1 the loop resolved nothing per witness. No test holds a witness with an unheld anchor (the only `Waiting::Anchor` test is goal/tests.rs:2173, a host fork).
first.fix: Change the code. In `predicate`, test `self.status(candidate.id(), proof) == Standing::Effective` before line 1103 and `continue` otherwise; an effective record always has a snapshot at its anchor (chain.rs:444-447), so the `?` can no longer fire for someone else's record. Add a goal test: under `open`, a declared result keeps counting while another member's review of it is held with an anchor that is not held, in both arrival orders of that review and the host record it names.
first.person_sees: Under the open and independent-attempts rules, a finished task goes back to unfinished on everyone's board and is offered to agents to start again. One member can do this to any result with a single record, and it stays that way even after that member is removed. With honest members it can happen briefly when a review arrives before the host record it was signed at.

first.title: Replay resolves rules, and re-validates the whole formation, once per (context, anchor), though nothing in the resolution reads the anchor
first.scenario: A goal of 200 tasks whose 50 members joined over time (about 55 host records). Honest daemons anchor at the head, so a task's start, result, reviews and review-request steps commonly sit at 2 to 4 anchors. Each replay then does roughly 400 to 800 full resolutions through `Verifier::resolve` where it did 202 before this commit. The bounds are one per context (every task inside one host-record interval) and one per rule-checked record (a host record between most work records). A task at subtask depth D pays D+1 formation validations per resolution. Expected: one resolution per context per replay, as before, with holders read at the anchor.

The parent recursion at rules.rs:138 uses the uncached `rules::resolve`. Since this commit nothing in `resolve`, `resolve_binding`, `inherit` or `narrows` reads `roles` or `only_member` (delegation.rs compares roles by name); they are only copied into the result at rules.rs:161-162, so every anchor of one context recomputes the same rules. (b) Cache the anchor-independent part by `Context` again and read holders and `only_member` from `chain.snapshot(anchor)` by reference when matching. Sharing the role map alone ends the holder copies but not the re-resolution; (b) ends both. Amend the plan's 'caches by `(Context, EventId)`' and the companion's 'cache keyed by `Context` alone is removed'. (c) Add a counter test in the style of `cutoff_traversals`, and a workload variant with admissions between tasks.

Two parts of the report need correcting: the deep copy on a cache hit was already there before this commit, and the cost does not grow with member count; it is a constant factor bounded by the number of records. Nothing was measured; all counts are by reading.
second.scenario:
200 top-level finished tasks, about 55 host records, honest daemons anchoring at the head.

Before the commit, per replay:
- about 202 misses in Verifier::resolve (one per context)
- plus about 200 uncached resolve_binding calls from task_binding, one per task-opening record
- so about 400 formation validations, not 202

After the commit, per replay:
- a floor of about 400 misses: each finished task resolves once at its records' anchor and once more at the head, because projection.rs:416 resolves every selected task at the head only to read its binding
- plus one miss for each (task, host record) pair where a member joined while the task was in flight, at most 55 times the number of tasks open at each join
- so about 400 to 650 misses and 600 to 850 validations, roughly 1.5 to 2 times the validations before; the reviewer's upper figure of 800 misses needs about 4 tasks in flight at every join

first.title: Each replay re-derives wanted review requests by scanning all held records per reviewer, and the new default asks every other member to review every result
first.scenario: A default goal (peer-review since this commit) with M members. A member posts a result. Every member but the author qualifies, so the author's daemon wants M-1 review requests, signs one per turn of `drive_flow` and replays the goal after each: M-1 replays per post. In each replay, for each of the U results still waiting on an open task and each of its M-1 reviewers, `insert` walks all held records and hashes an effect identity for every held step record until it finds a match. With S step records held (S grows by M-1 per result) that is about U x (M-1) x S hashes per replay. At 50 members and 200 results (S near 5,000) one post is about 49 replays and about 12 million hashes for that result alone. Under the earlier default, `open`, no request was wanted. Expected: the arm reads what the projection has just computed.

first.title: A waiting join cannot be re-run without retyping the same --name, and a chosen name cannot be corrected
first.scenario: A person runs `locust --owner goal join --ticket-file t --agent codex-maple-1a2b3c4d` with no --name. The host's computer is off, so the agent is joining under its enrolled name. They re-run the same command with `--name Maple` (or the reverse: first with --name, then without, for example to add `--level ask`). The CLI always sends a name, falling back to the enrolled one. The daemon compares it with the stored one and answers conflict (exit 7): "the pending admission already has a different name". The level is not changed either. Nothing prints which name is pending, and the person cannot drop the waiting join. If the ticket was already refused, this check still runs first, so the person is told about a name instead of being told to ask for a new invitation.
first.evidence: invitations.rs:317-321 returns the conflict before the refused check at 322-326 and before the level rewrite at 327-341, which is the branch that exists so a re-run can apply. only_you.rs:918 calls `member_name` (138-161), which substitutes the enrolled name when --name is absent, so the daemon cannot tell "not given" from "given". `join.name` is read only at peers.rs:248 and here; no view exposes it. `goal_leave` needs membership (goals.rs:463) and `join_delete` is written only by `finish_joins` (commit.rs:383). The plan (line 2589-2596) says only that goal_join takes the name, stores it and re-signs with it; this refusal is the builder's addition and has no test.
first.fix: Code should change. On a retry with the same ticket, keep the stored name unless the person gave --name (make the name optional on goal.join, or have the CLI omit it). When --name is given while still waiting, replace the stored name, and drop `member.name == request.name` at peers.rs:334 so a retry after the host already admitted is still answered. Move the refused check ahead of the name check. Add one sentence to the plan saying which of these it is.
first.person_sees: Re-running the join command while waiting for the host fails with "the pending admission already has a different name" unless they type exactly the same --name as before. A name they defaulted or mistyped cannot be changed before admission, and after admission it is signed into the goal.

second.statement: Real, but smaller than claimed: while a join waits for the host, re-running `goal join` with the same ticket and a different name (given or defaulted) is refused with conflict, and no command can change or drop the waiting name. The level can still be changed with `level set`, the person was shown the name before it was stored, and the name being fixed after admission is the plan's own assumption 8, so severity is low.
second.scenario:
1. Host's computer is off. The person runs `locust --owner goal join --ticket-file t --agent codex-maple-1a2b3c4d` with no --name. The plan reads "Join ... as codex-maple-1a2b3c4d"; they confirm. The daemon stores a JoinRecord with that name and prints "Joining ... as codex-maple-1a2b3c4d".
2. They re-run with `--name Maple`, or the reverse order (first `--name Maple`, later without it, since `member_name` substitutes the enrolled name). `Node::goal_join` finds the same-ticket pending join, sees `join.name != name` and returns conflict, exit 7: "the pending admission already has a different name". The message does not say which name is waiting and no later view shows it.
3. No way out while waiting: `goal leave` answers unavailable for a joining agent, a different ticket answers "another invitation is being redeemed", and nothing deletes the JoinRecord except admission. When the host returns, the agent is admitted under the first name for good.
4. Corrections to the finding: `level set` works for a joining agent, so the level is not stuck; the name was printed by the plan and the result of the first run; if the ticket was refused and the name differs, the join command gives the name message, but `status` still says the invitation was refused and to ask for a fresh one, and a fresh ticket after a refusal does take a new name.
second.fix: Code should change, and the plan should gain one sentence saying a waiting join can be re-run with another name. Smallest change, in `Node::goal_join` (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/invitations.rs:313-341): test `join.refused` first, then on a same-ticket retry write the JoinRecord again with the requested name beside the level write instead of returning conflict. That treats the name the way this branch already treats the level (a re-run applies what the command says, default included); `joins()` re-signs from the stored record on the next exchange. With that, `plan_join` (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:331-335) must drop `member.name == request.name` from the already-redeemed branch, otherwise a rename that races the host's admission is refused, the joiner is marked refused and stops asking. Add one node test for a same-ticket re-run with a new name and one for the refused order. Making the request's name optional so an omitted --name keeps the stored one is a nicer variant but not needed to close this.
second.person_sees: While waiting for the host's computer, running the join command again fails with "the pending admission already has a different name" unless the name matches the first run exactly, including when --name was simply left off or added. A name picked or defaulted on the first run cannot be changed before the host admits the agent, and after that the goal keeps it for good unless the host removes and re-invites the agent. Nothing is lost otherwise: the join still goes through and the level can be changed with `level set`.

second.statement: `goal add` for an agent that is already a member still shows the full "Add X to "G" as NAME, a ROLE, at level L" plan, built from --name or the enrolled name, the --role or default counting role, and the selected level, and after yes changes nothing and prints "NAME is already a member" with that typed or enrolled name instead of the signed one. `goal join` with a ticket for an agent already in the goal does the same thing: its plan says "Join ... as NAME ... Joins as a ROLE." and the result prints "NAME joined", while the daemon changed nothing and the ticket stays unused.

first.title: One member's record with an unknown anchor stops a declared result from counting on every computer
first.scenario: A goal follows `open` (the same holds for `independent-attempts`, the `ship` step of `pipeline`, a custom rule with a `declaration` part, and the shared files of an `open` goal, which this commit puts under the goal's rule). Juniper posts result S and declares it done; S counts everywhere. Maple, an ordinary member whose computer is modified or buggy, signs one `review_recorded` (an opinion, which this commit makes legal) or `completion_declared` that names S and whose header `anchor` is an id that is no governance record anyone holds. Header::check only asks that an anchor is present (event.rs:821), screen keeps any record by an admitted author (screen.rs:36-41), so every computer holds it. From then on `approval(S)` returns an error on every computer: S shows as not counting, the task round is no longer completed, the lead's pick of S is refused because `scope_select` has no evidence to pin (tasks.rs:300), `workspace integrate` answers `exact workspace candidate lacks required evidence` (requests/workspace.rs:558), and a stage that waits on that completion can stay shut (flow.rs:210 passes the error on). Removing Maple does not help, because the record stays held and indexed. The honest version is a flicker: a computer that receives a member's opinion before the governance record it anchors on shows the result as not counting until that record arrives.

Line 1103 then runs `self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?` before the standing test at line 1147. `resolve` answers `Err(Pending(Anchor))` when the anchor has no snapshot (fold.rs:116-119) and the `?` returns that from `predicate` and `approval`. projection.rs:209-210 turns the error into `approved = false`. Before this commit eligibility was read from the subject's rules and a witness that was not effective was skipped by `eligible && status == Effective`. `Reviews` and `Check` rules are safe, because `latest_review` keeps only effective records (fold.rs:1039), so the default `peer-review` goal is not affected. docs/formations.md:188-189 says a waiting record `is never counted as a rejection`; here it is. No test holds a witness whose anchor is missing.

In `predicate`, skip a witness that is not effective before resolving at its anchor: move the `self.status(candidate.id(), proof) == Standing::Effective` test above line 1103, or `continue` when the candidate's anchor has no snapshot. Add a replay test in goal/tests.rs: under `open`, a declared result keeps counting when another member's review or declaration of it names an anchor nobody holds, forward, reversed and reloaded.

first.scenario: One person runs two agents on the host's computer, Maple (the host's agent) and Juniper, in a `peer-review` goal. Juniper posts result S on an open task and nobody approves it. Juniper's daemon will not sign for an agent that left, and replay would exclude a record by a non-member at the head, so the step can never be signed. Every later `goal add`, join or `role give` that creates a new eligible reviewer adds one more such step per unapproved result of Juniper's.

S is still effective, does not count, and its task is open, so none of the new filters drop it; Cedar's request has a new effect id because `target_slot` is the recipient. `drive_flow` cannot sign it (node/flow.rs:24-32), and `stalled` reports it as `RunnerLeft` or `RunnerNotMember` (requests/levels.rs:100-128), which `goal status` prints as `Step ... stalled for ...`. Before this commit `review_templates` read the members at the result's own anchor, so nothing new was wanted after the author had gone. Cedar still sees S in `to_review`, so no work waits.
first.fix: Code should change. In `desired_effects`, do not want a review request whose runner is not a member at the head. For an author that left and is not yet removed, leave review requests out of `stalled`: the new reviewer already has the result in `to_review`. Add a node test: an agent with an unapproved result leaves, a member is added, and `goal status` lists no stalled step.

Two parts of the report are wrong: the line is not permanent (it clears when the result is approved, the task is revised, or the agent is re-admitted), and the proposed fix would leave `Stall::RunnerLeft` and `Stall::RunnerNotMember` with no producer and break a pinned test.

The test gives lead to Maple, takes it back, and only then asserts roles["lead"] == [host] and that status.deciding contains lead. Suppose role_change read the role's kind from the current definition, which the plan forbids. Then give would add (holders [host, Maple]) and take would leave [host]: the same final state. status.deciding comes from goal_status, not from role_change, so that assertion still passes too.
first.evidence: roles.rs:199-210 has no assertion between the give and the take. The replace-or-add choice is at goals.rs:331-335 (`if deciding { next.clear(); }`). The other give test (roles.rs:118) runs under current rules. goal/tests.rs a_role_list_outlives_the_binding... signs RoleHolders by hand, so it does not test the daemon's choice. The cli.rs test uses a stub daemon.
first.fix: After the give, assert status.roles["lead"] == vec![member]. Also assert that a stale `expected` of [host] is then a conflict.
first.person_sees: nothing visible

second.statement: role_give_and_take_work_on_a_role_only_earlier_rules_declare (crates/locust-core/src/node/tests/roles.rs:199-210) checks the lead's holders only after the give and the take have both run, so it never pins the plan's "role.give replaces the lead" for a role only earlier rules declare. The shipped code does replace; the gap is in the test only.
second.scenario:
1. The goal starts under `directed` (lead = [host]), Maple joins, and the rules are rebound to `peer-review`, which declares no roles (presets.rs:59-60).
2. Suppose role_change took the role's kind from the current definition instead of Self::deciding (goals.rs:321). Then `deciding` is false for lead and the give signs RoleHolders [host, Maple].
3. Replay accepts that record. chain.rs:184-196 checks only that holders are non-empty, sorted and admitted. The exactly-one-holder check at chain.rs:557-576 runs only when rules are bound.
4. The test's `change` helper reads `expected` from live state (roles.rs:75), so the take of Maple matches [host, Maple] and signs [host].
5. The final asserts all pass: roles["lead"] == [host], status.deciding contains lead (goals.rs:398 computes it from deciding_known, independent of role_change), and the same after restart.

One narrowing: because role_change and goal_status share deciding_known, a regression inside that helper (reading only the current binding) would fail the status.deciding assert. Only a regression in role_change's own choice of source slips through.
second.fix:
In role_give_and_take_work_on_a_role_only_earlier_rules_declare, add one assertion between the two `change` calls: `assert_eq!(status(&mut d, owner, goal).roles["lead"], vec![member]);`.

Drop the proposed stale-`expected` conflict assertion. It does not tell replace from add, because [host] is stale in both cases, and the compare-and-set at goals.rs:311-315 runs before the kind is read. It is already pinned at roles.rs:127-133. No change to the plan or to production code.
second.person_sees: Nothing today: giving the lead of an older rule set to someone does replace the previous lead. The risk is a future change that leaves a goal with two leads on a role the current rules no longer mention, with no test catching it.

first.title: A rules binding refused for a named member who is not in the goal is reported as a role with the wrong number of holders
first.scenario: A hand-written formation names one specific member's key as the picker, `selection: {kind: participant, key: K}`. The host runs `goal create --formation-json` with it, where K is not the host's agent, or `rules bind` after K's member was removed. validate_binding excludes the binding because K is not in snapshot.members. advance turns the exclusion into the answer `conflict: a role that picks or closes must have exactly one holder`. No role is involved. Before this commit the sentence was "an authority must bind exactly one admitted principal", which was true for both cases. The plan's companion asked for the rename.
first.evidence: chain.rs:557-577: authority_ok covers Authority::Role and Authority::Participant, and both fail with the one string. node/commit.rs:346-359 returns exclusion.reason() as the Conflict message. Neither goal_create nor rules_bind checks a participant's membership first.
first.fix: Split the exclusion: keep the role sentence for Authority::Role, and return "a member named to pick or close is not in this goal" for Authority::Participant. Correct the companion's line to match.
first.person_sees: "conflict: a role that picks or closes must have exactly one holder" when their rules name one specific member who is not in the goal. That points them at roles, and there are none to fix.

second.statement: validate_binding refuses a rules binding for two different causes with one sentence: a deciding role with other than one holder, and a decider named by key who is not a member. Since 8c086c1 that sentence is "a role that picks or closes must have exactly one holder", which is untrue for the named-key case; the code follows the companion's requested rename word for word, so the gap is in the plan text as much as the code.
second.scenario: 1. Host writes a formation with `"selection": {"kind": "participant", "key": K}` (or `finish`, or `workspace.integrator`), K a well-formed 64-hex key. 2a. `locust --owner goal create --formation-json ...` where K is not the host's own agent: the CLI (only_you.rs chosen_formation/create_plan) and the daemon's checked_definition only check that K parses (organization/validation.rs:45-49, 88). goal_create signs genesis, the host's admission and RulesBound with sign_at, with no trial replay. 2b. Or `rules bind` in an existing goal where K was never admitted or was removed: rules_bind checks only the role kind (deciding / is_authority_role) and signs with self.author, again with no trial. 3. On commit, advance replays; validate_binding's authority_ok returns false for Authority::Participant because snapshot.members lacks K, and the single exclusion string is returned. 4. advance turns it into ApiError Conflict with exclusion.reason(); the CLI prints `conflict: a role that picks or closes must have exactly one holder`. Nothing is stored (rollback), so for 2a no goal is created.
second.fix: In validate_binding (crates/locust-core/src/goal/chain.rs:556-577), stop folding both arms into one bool: return the existing sentence only when an Authority::Role fails, and a second Precondition such as "a member named to pick or close is not in this goal" when an Authority::Participant fails (the same list also covers workspace.integrator, so the wording may want to cover accepting shared files too). Add one replay test beside rules_bound_fills_unheld_declared_roles_with_the_host_and_requires_one_holder_per_authority for the non-member key case, and amend docs/roles-and-permissions-plan-details.md:235 (and the verification row at :298 if desired) to name both sentences. Code and companion both change; no behaviour change beyond the text.
second.person_sees: A host who hand-writes rules naming one specific member's key to pick, close or accept files, and that key is not in the goal, is told "conflict: a role that picks or closes must have exactly one holder". Their rules have no role to fix, so the message sends them looking in the wrong place; the goal is not created or the rules are not changed, and nothing else is lost. Only hand-written formations hit this; the built-in formations and the CLI's own shared-files path (which names the host's agent, who cannot be removed) do not.

Nothing is lost and nothing is recorded, but the message sends them to look at roles and holders when the real cause is that the named member is not in the goal.

first.title: A member whose role was taken can still approve results posted after the take; only picks and closes have a bound that stops this
first.scenario: Goal under `directed` (count 1) or `review-panel`. Maple is the host's agent, Juniper was given `reviewer`, Cedar is a member. Juniper's newest record is anchored at governance position 7. At position 8 the host runs `role take --member Juniper reviewer`. Cedar's daemon holds position 8 and posts result R anchored there. Juniper's computer runs a changed daemon and signs an approval of R whose anchor is position 7. Replay on every computer finds the approval effective and counts it, so under `directed` R shows as approved on Juniper's approval alone. `member remove` afterwards keeps it, because the removal's cutoff is Juniper's latest effective record. It should be excluded: the approval is anchored before the result it approves, which an unmodified daemon never signs.
first.evidence: Read, not run. fold.rs:563-590 judges a review with resolve(context, its own anchor) and compares nothing with the subject's anchor; the same holds for CheckAttested (591) and CompletionDeclared (540), and WorkOffered (339) passes active_context for a task opened later because current_round (792) starts from the opening record whatever its anchor. chain.rs:486-494 only stops an author's own anchors going backward. commitments.rs:417-426 already excludes a pick or close whose round, subject or evidence is anchored after it ("proof uses governance after the decision anchor"), so the bound exists for decisions only. An honest daemon anchors at its head (goal/mod.rs:270-284) and can review only a result whose anchor it holds, so the bound would exclude nothing honest. goal/tests.rs:2816-2836 covers only a result that existed before the change. node/requests/goals.rs:513-524 picks the removal cutoff. The plan names the general risk at roles-and-permissions-plan.md:3119-3127 ("keeps reviewing there until the host removes the member") and says at 3124-3125 that going backward is the only bound, which is not so for picks and closes.
first.fix: Change the code, then the plan's risk note. In `check`, exclude a ReviewRecorded, CheckAttested or CompletionDeclared whose anchor position is lower than its subject's anchor position, and consider the same test for an offer, a start and a result against the record that opened their round. Add a replay test beside the ex-holder test: result posted after the role change, approval anchored before it, excluded forward and reversed. first.title: One malformed record from any member stops a result from counting under a declaration rule
first.scenario: Goal under `open` (also `independent-attempts`, the `ship` stage of `pipeline`, or any formation whose completion is a Declaration). Member A publishes result X and declares it done, so X counts. Member M, with a modified daemon, signs a ReviewRecorded, CompletionDeclared or CheckAttested with subject X whose header anchor is any id that is not a record on the host's chain (X's own id will do). Header::check passes because the anchor is Some, screen keeps it because M was admitted, and its standing is Pending(Waiting::Anchor) for good. On every computer `approval(X, None, None)` now returns Err and X shows as not approved; the round is no longer completed. It should ignore a witness that is not effective and keep counting A's declaration. The same happens for a short time with no hostile member: another member's review or declaration of X anchored at a governance record this computer has not received yet un-approves X here until that record arrives. Removing M does not clear it, since the record stays held and indexed.
first.evidence: fold.rs:53-59 indexes every held witness by subject with no standing test. In `predicate`, lines 1091-1101 filter by `latest_review` (effective only) for Reviews and Check, but line 1097 `_ => Some(candidate.id())` lets every candidate through for a Declaration rule. Line 1103 `let resolved = self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?;` runs before the effectiveness test further down, and `resolve` (fold.rs:112-119) returns `Err(Standing::Pending(Waiting::Anchor))` when `chain.snapshot(&anchor)` is None. The `?` leaves the whole predicate. projection.rs:209 turns that into not approved with `.ok().flatten()`; flow.rs:211 propagates it into stage readiness. Before this commit `predicate` used the `resolved` passed in and a pending witness simply failed the `status == Effective` test (git show 8c086c1^:crates/locust-core/src/goal/fold.rs, predicate). No test holds a witness whose anchor has no snapshot.
first.fix: Change the code, not the plan. In `predicate`, test `self.status(candidate.id(), proof) == Standing::Effective` before line 1103 and `continue` when it is not; an effective record's anchor always has a snapshot, so the resolve can then no longer fail for a reason the candidate chose. Add a signed replay test in goal/tests.rs: under `open`, an author-declared result stays approved while another member's declaration and review of it name an anchor that is not a governance record, forward and reversed.
first.person_sees: In a goal where a member's own word makes a result count, a finished result flips back to not done for everyone and its task shows as open to take again, after one bad record from any member. Removing that member does not bring the result back. On a computer that is still syncing, the same flip can appear briefly and then clear.

second.statement: Under any completion rule that is a Declaration (`open`, `independent-attempts`, the ship task of `pipeline`, and shared-file changes that inherit that rule), one held review, declaration or check record about a result whose anchor is not a record on the host's chain makes `Verifier::predicate` return an error, so the result stops counting on every computer and stays that way. This is a regression introduced by 8c086c1: the per-candidate `resolve(...)?` runs before the candidate's effectiveness test.
second.scenario:
1. Goal under `open` (Formation::default, completion = Declaration by the result's author; presets.rs:30, organization.rs:218-223). Member A publishes X and declares it; X is approved and its round completed.
2. Member M, with a modified daemon, signs CompletionDeclared (or ReviewRecorded / CheckAttested) with subject X and header anchor = X's own id (any id that is not a governance record works). Header::check only requires the anchor to be Some (event.rs:821). screen keeps it because M was admitted (screen.rs:36-44). History never drops events.
3. On every computer Verifier::new indexes it under X with no standing test (fold.rs:53-59). In predicate, allowed is None and the rule is a Declaration, so `_ => Some(candidate.id())` (fold.rs:1097) lets it through; `self.resolve(context, candidate.header().anchor.unwrap())?` (fold.rs:1103) finds no snapshot and returns Err(Pending(Waiting::Anchor)) (fold.rs:116-119), leaving the whole predicate before A's declaration is counted.
4. projection.rs:209 turns the Err into approved = false with empty evidence and `round.completed |= approved` stays false; the same at :236 for document revisions and :262 for shared-file proposals. task_available (goal/mod.rs:435) reports the task as takeable again. Under `independent-attempts` the lead's pick is built from that empty evidence (requests/tasks.rs:296-304), so the pick fails with Waiting::Evidence (fold.rs:979-984) and X cannot be picked; a shared-file proposal M targets is refused at requests/workspace.rs:556.
5. Removing M changes nothing: the record stays in history, stays indexed, and its anchor still has no snapshot. M can repeat it for every result.
Corrections to the original wording: (a) the flow.rs:210 propagation into stage readiness is not reached by the built-in `pipeline`, because ship requires draft's completion and draft uses Reviews/Contribution, where latest_review already filters to effective records; it applies to custom formations whose required stage completes by declaration. (b) The no-hostile-member transient is narrower than stated: a sync exchange sends the governance log first (sync/outbox.rs:14-29), so it needs a relay that itself holds the member's record without the governance record it names. Results already picked are unaffected (pinned path, projection.rs:363).
second.fix: Change the code, not the plan. first.title: The rules-bind plan's count of file changes to propose again includes changes that need no re-proposal, and the host's agent cannot re-propose first files
first.scenario: (a) Two members propose on the same head; one lands, the other goes stale, and its author composes a successor that lands. The stale original is still un-integrated in the epoch. The next `rules bind` plan prints "1 file changes that have not landed must be proposed again by their authors", though that work already landed. Proposals replay excluded are counted too, so a hostile member can inflate the number at will. (b) The host ran `workspace init --publish` and has not yet run `workspace integrate --expected-empty`, then runs `rules bind`. The stranded change is the first files, whose author is the host's agent.
first.evidence: only_you.rs:1309-1316 counts every proposal with `context.round == epoch && integrated_as.is_empty()`. `workspace_proposals` (requests/workspace.rs:449-461) lists every held `WorkspaceProposed` whatever its standing or staleness. For (b): after the bind, the daemon signs an `Unseeded` epoch (goals.rs:225-231). The agent cannot post a change with no parent (requests/workspace.rs:989-993). `workspace propose` needs a checkout, and none can exist while there is no accepted tree. Only the person re-running `workspace init` works (cli/workspace.rs:383-441 accepts an existing unseeded epoch).
first.fix: Change both plan and code. Count only effective, non-stale proposals whose parent is the current head. When the stranded change has no parent, say that the host shares the first files again with `workspace init`.
first.person_sees: A plan that says more file changes must be redone than is true. After the rules change, a host whose starting folder had not landed is told its "author" must propose it again, when in fact they must run `workspace init` once more.

second.statement: The `rules bind` plan (and its result, which repeats the line) counts every held proposal of the current epoch that has no revision of its own, so it includes losers of a race whose work already landed through a successor, and proposals that replay excludes. When the only stranded change is the host's not-yet-accepted first files, the line tells the host that the "author" must propose again, but only the person re-running `workspace init` can do that. The code follows the plan's own wording (plan line 2648-2650), so this is a flaw in the plan that the code inherited, not a builder departure.
second.scenario: (a) Epoch E, head H0. Members A and B each publish a change on H0. A's is integrated (head R1). B's proposal Pb is now stale; B runs `workspace compose --source Pb` (or updates and proposes afresh), and that successor is integrated (head R2). Pb still has no revision naming it, and its round is E. The host runs `locust --owner rules bind --formation peer-review --plan`: `rules_plan` counts Pb and prints "1 file changes that have not landed must be proposed again by their authors." Nothing needs proposing again. Every lost race in the epoch's life adds one more, and so does any proposal a member signs that replay excludes or leaves pending, because `workspace_proposals` lists held records whatever their standing. (b) The host runs `workspace init --root ... --publish` (epoch E1, unseeded, seed proposal P by the host's agent, parent none) and, before `workspace integrate --expected-empty`, runs `rules bind`. The plan prints the same "1 file changes ... by their authors" line. The daemon signs epoch E2 with checkpoint Unseeded. P cannot land in E2 (`integrate` answers "proposal must be composed against the exact expected epoch and head"; `compose` needs an accepted revision and refuses seed sources). The agent cannot post a parentless change (denied without the owner's act) and cannot have a folder to propose from, since registering or connecting one needs an accepted tree. The only way forward is the person running `workspace init` again, which accepts an existing ready unseeded epoch.
second.fix: Change both the plan sentence (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:2648-2650) and `rules_plan` in crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs (filter at 1309-1314, text at 1316). When a counted proposal has `parent == None` (the tree has no files yet), print instead that the first files have not landed and the host shares them again with `locust --owner workspace init`. While there, print "1 file change ... its author" for a count of one. A member can still post many live changes on the head, but then the number is true. Add a CLI test with a stale and an excluded proposal in the `WorkspaceProposals` answer (the existing test at crates/locust/tests/cli.rs:2968 returns an empty list, so nothing pins the count today).

If the host had shared a starting folder but not yet accepted it, the message points at their agent, which cannot redo it; nothing tells them the real step is to run `workspace init` once more, and the errors they meet when they try to accept or compose the old change do not say so either.

first.title: A picker named by key who is not a member is refused with a sentence about a role
first.scenario: `goal create --formation-json` (or `rules bind`) with a hand-written formation that has no roles and names a teammate's agent key as the one who picks (`selection: participant`). Through the host's own daemon the role arm cannot fire: a new role starts with the host's agent, and `rules_bind`'s kind check (goals.rs:162-176) refuses first. Nothing tells them the real cause: the agent they named has to be a member of the goal first (so a new goal cannot name a teammate as picker at all until that teammate has joined). first.title: One record with an unknown anchor stops a result from counting under any rule with a declaration part
first.scenario: Goal under `open` (or `independent-attempts`, or any formation whose completion rule has a `declaration` part; also a shared tree whose rule is the author's declaration). first.scenario: A peer-review goal has the host's agent and four members. The host runs `rules bind --formation review-panel`. Replay starts the `reviewer` list with the host's agent only (chain.rs:538). Every result under the new rules needs two approvals from reviewers other than its author, so none can count: a member's result can get at most the host agent's one approval, and the host agent's own result none. Members' agents see nothing to review. The plan and the result of `rules bind` print no reviewers line. `goal status` then prints `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.`, which points the host at adding people, not at `role give` for the four who are already there. The plan's goal paragraph promises that where the counting rule needs reviewers the host's agent cannot supply alone, 'the work does not wait for the host to give roles'; decision 18 rejected exactly this outcome for new goals. The plan only covers `goal add` and `goal invite`.

Open tasks keep their old rules until revised.` plus file lines only. goals.rs `rules_bind` signs the binding (and an epoch) and no role record. chain.rs:536-539 fills a newly declared role with the host only. presentation.rs:618 prints the add-or-invite hint whatever the member count.

first.title: Binding review-panel rules on a goal that already has members leaves only the host's agent as reviewer, and neither the plan nor the result says so
first.scenario: Goal "Parser cleanup" follows peer-review with three members: Harbor (host's agent), Maple, Juniper. The person runs `locust --owner rules bind --goal "Parser cleanup" --formation review-panel` and says yes. Replay starts the new `reviewer` list holding only Harbor. From then on every result under the current rules needs 2 approvals from reviewers who did not write it, and one reviewer exists, so nothing can count until the person runs `role give` twice. The plan prints only `Bind "Parser cleanup" (..) to review-panel. Open tasks keep their old rules until revised.` and the result only `"Parser cleanup" now follows review-panel. ...`. `goal status` then prints `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.`, which points at adding new members, not at Maple and Juniper who are already in (`goal add` for them answers `is already a member` and gives no role).
first.evidence: rules_plan builds its text at only_you.rs:1326-1334 with no reviewers line; roles::initial_reviewers is called only from create_plan (only_you.rs:578). chain.rs validate_binding (lines 536-539) gives a newly declared role `vec![host]` and nothing else. The only hint is presentation.rs:618. The plan's Goal paragraph (2289-2291) promises that work does not wait for the host to give roles, but only covers `goal add` and `goal invite` (2683-2694); the code follows the plan.
first.fix: The plan should change, then the code. Smallest: when the formation being bound has a counting role whose list will be short, the `rules bind` plan and result print the holders now, how many more are needed, and the `role give` command for each current member; the status line names `role give` for members already in. Owner's call whether the one yes of `rules bind` should also give that role to the current members.
first.person_sees: After switching a running team to review-panel, results silently stop counting and the agents' work waits. Nothing in the command says the person must now run `role give`, and `goal status` suggests adding more members instead.

second.statement: Binding a formation with a counting role (review-panel) onto a goal that already has members starts the `reviewer` list with only the host's agent, and neither the `rules bind` plan nor its result says so; `goal status` then points at adding or inviting members, which does nothing for members already in. The code follows the plan as written; the plan covers this only for `goal create`, `goal add` and `goal invite`, and no declared departure touches it.
second.scenario: 1. `goal create --title "Parser cleanup"` with no formation uses peer-review, which declares no roles (presets.rs: `peer_review` has only `peer_completion()`), so state.roles is empty. 2. Maple and Juniper are added; `roles::selected_role` finds no counting role under peer-review (roles.rs:89-109), so they get none. 3. `locust --owner rules bind --goal "Parser cleanup" --formation review-panel`: the plan prints only `Bind "Parser cleanup" (..) to review-panel. Open tasks keep their old rules until revised.` (plus shared-files lines when a tree is on). 4. On yes, `rules_bind` in goals.rs signs the binding (and a workspace epoch if the tree is on) and no role record; replay's `validate_binding` gives the new role `vec![host]` (chain.rs:536-539). 5. Result prints only `"Parser cleanup" now follows review-panel. ...`. 6. From here: tasks opened or revised after the bind need 2 reviewer approvals not by the author, and one reviewer exists, so their results cannot count; if shared files are on they moved to the same rule in the same command, so no file change can land either. Tasks already open keep peer-review and still count (a correction to the reviewer's "results stop counting"). 7. `goal status` prints `2 more reviewers are needed; members you add or invite become reviewers.`; `goal add` for Maple answers `Maple is already a member of ...` and gives no role (only_you.rs:771-780). 8. Only `role give` fixes it. One give (Maple) already lets Juniper's results count; two are needed before every member's results can count (a correction to "nothing can count until twice").
second.fix: Plan first, then code. Smallest: in `rules_plan` (crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs), when `roles::counting_role(&formation)` is Some and `roles::missing_reviewers` is above zero for the holders the role will have after the bind (the list in `observed.roles`, or the host's agent alone when the role has no list yet), append a line with the reviewers after the bind, how many more are needed, and one `locust --owner role give --goal G --member KEYPREFIX reviewer` line per current member who does not hold it; `rules_bind` repeats it in the result. The command never says the person now has to make the existing members reviewers, and goal status suggests adding or inviting members, which does not help for members who are already in.

first.scenario: Goal follows `open` (completion is the author's own declaration; the same holds for `independent-attempts`, the `ship` step of `pipeline`, and any rule with a Declaration part). Member B's computer signs a ReviewRecorded, CompletionDeclared or CheckAttested that names R and whose header anchor is not a record on the host's chain: a made-up id from a modified or buggy daemon, a governance record this computer has not received yet, or one cut by a governance fork (the case the K1 review lists at chain.rs:451). B is admitted, so every computer keeps the record (goal/screen.rs:35-43, node/replica.rs:210-216). From then on Verifier::approval(R, None, None) returns Err instead of the evidence, on every computer that holds B's record. It should ignore a witness that is not effective and keep counting R on A's declaration, as it did before this commit.

Verifier::resolve returns Err(Pending(Waiting::Anchor)) when the chain has no snapshot for that anchor (fold.rs:116-119), and the `?` aborts the whole predicate. Before 8c086c1 the loop used the caller's resolved rules and such a witness was simply skipped. The record stays in history after B is removed, so removal does not undo it. No test covers a witness with an unheld anchor.

first.scenario: A review-panel goal, where `goal add` and `goal invite` carry `reviewer` by default. Each admission appends the new member to the list in replay, with no bound. The header costs about 153 bytes before the keys, so (16384 - 153) / 32 gives 507 holders. api.rs:1975-1983 maps the error to `invalid` with the text `header exceeds the admitted size`. The plan's Risks note bounds a role name by the header limit but says nothing about the holder list. The K1 review reports the same 16 KiB bound for stage recipients; this is a new record kind with the same limit. Unlike that case, nothing here is signed unattended, so only the person's command fails.

first.scenario: Juniper's key starts 8d03f2b6. The host runs `role take --member Juniper reviewer` and gets `Undo: locust --owner role give --goal 7f3a9c1e --member 8d03f2b6 reviewer`. The host re-runs the Undo line. resolve_member finds no member key starting 8d03f2b6 (goal.status lists active members only), falls through to member_by_name, and returns Mallory; role.give makes Mallory a reviewer and prints a normal-looking result. It should answer not_found: a key-shaped selector should never resolve through a name another person chose.
first.evidence: selectors.rs:97-112 tries key prefixes only `if !matches.is_empty()`, then line 113 `member_by_name(&observed.members, value)` runs for the same hex-shaped value. It never has a member whose name equals another member's key prefix, so it passes unchanged if resolve_member tried names before key prefixes. The only end-to-end prefix use (cli.rs:2581, printed `--member 03030303`) has no hex-shaped names. The plan relies on this order: an Undo line names the member 'by a prefix of its key ... never by its name, which another person chose'.

Move the key/prefix/name steps into a pure function over the member list, as member_by_name is, and assert: with V (key 8d03f2b6...) and M named "8d03f2b6", "8d03f2b6" resolves to V; with V absent it is not_found.
first.person_sees: After a member is removed, an old Undo or role command the host re-runs can land on a different member who chose that member's key prefix as its name. The impostor gets the role and the output looks normal.

No test pins the order: the unit test named for it only calls `member_by_name`, and neither CLI test has a hex-shaped name. With Juniper's full key the daemon would have answered conflict "not a member". 5. The scan this replaced made one pass for all candidates and read the standings the fold had already computed. first.title: Joining again under another name answers 'joined' with the new name while the goal keeps the old one
first.scenario: claude-juniper is already a member, admitted as 'Juniper' (`goal add --name Juniper`, or an earlier join with `--name`). Its owner runs `locust --owner goal join --agent claude-juniper TICKET` again with no `--name`, so the name defaults to the enrolled one. The plan prints `Join "Parser cleanup" (7f3a9c1e) as claude-juniper-77aa0c52.` After the yes the daemon takes the already-a-member branch, ignores `name`, and answers `Joined { membership: Member }`. The command prints `claude-juniper-77aa0c52 joined "Parser cleanup" · auto.` The signed name is still Juniper and `goal status` shows Juniper. The same request while the admission is still pending is refused as `conflict`, so the two branches disagree. `goal add` has the same slip in its own text: it prints the requested name in '... is already a member of ...'.
first.evidence: invitations.rs:294-311 returns `Response::Joined` with `Tx::none()` and no comparison with `entry.state().members[&principal].name`. invitations.rs:317-321 refuses the pending case with 'the pending admission already has a different name'. crates/locust/src/cli/only_you.rs:885 (the plan sentence) and :957 (`format!("{name} joined \"{title}\" · {}.", ...)`) print the requested name; :774 prints it in the already-a-member line of `goal add`. `Response::Joined` carries no member name, so the command cannot print the signed one.
first.fix: In the already-a-member branch compare the signed name with `name`. Either answer `conflict` as the pending branch does, or keep the no-op and have the command line print the name from `goal.status`. In `add_plan` and `join_plan`, when the agent is already a member, show the name it carries rather than the requested one.
first.person_sees: The plan and the result say the agent joined under one name, while the goal and every other member keep showing the name it was first admitted with.

second.statement: When an agent that is already a member repeats `goal join` (or `goal add`) with a name different from its signed one, the daemon's already-a-member branch ignores the name and answers `Joined { membership: Member }`, and the command line prints the requested name in both the plan and the result. The signed name is unchanged, and the same repeat while admission is still pending is refused as `conflict`, so the two branches added/kept by this commit disagree.
second.scenario:
1. claude-juniper-77aa0c52 is admitted to "Parser cleanup" with no `--name`, so its signed name is its enrolled name (or the reverse: admitted as Juniper, repeated with no `--name`).

What I verified by reading:
(1) `Verifier::resolve` (fold.rs:112) now caches by (context, anchor) where it cached by context alone. On a miss it calls `rules::resolve` (rules.rs:30), then `resolve_binding` (rules.rs:113), which runs `valid_definition` (goal/mod.rs:44). That serializes the formation to JSON and runs the full `organization::inspect` (parse, validate, normalize, hash). For a subtask, `resolve_binding` recurses into the parent through the uncached `rules::resolve`, so a miss at depth D pays D inspections.
(2) Every cache hit returns `.cloned()`, a deep copy of `Resolved` including `EffectiveRules.roles`, the whole role map. Under review-panel the default counting role holds every added member.
(3) `desired_effects` (flow.rs:370-515) now, for each effective published result or document revision that does not yet count, filters and sorts the whole `history.events` for decisions in that context, after an `approval` call. `stage_ready` (flow.rs:108) resolves at each matching review's anchor.
(4) The only performance workload, tests/organization_performance.rs, anchors every event at one rules binding with two admissions, is `#[ignore]`d and has no gate. It cannot see any per-anchor cost.

Please work out by reading:
- How many distinct (context, anchor) keys a realistic goal produces. Every admission, role give or take, epoch, rules bind and host task revise is a new anchor, and honest daemons anchor at the head. Take for example 50 members joining over the life of 200 tasks.
- The cost of one miss and one hit.
- How often a `Verifier` and its cache are rebuilt: per fold, per request, per `pending` item (views.rs and `Goal::latest_reviews`), per `drive_flow` in node/flow.rs.
- Whether `desired_effects` is now quadratic in held events for a goal with many uncounted results, and how often the node calls it.

Report growth orders with the multiplying factors and the call sites, and say whether validating a definition once per binding per fold, or sharing the role map, would remove the cost. critic.reason:
Coverage is adequate apart from one gap: nobody sized the replay cost of the new per-anchor rules resolution, so I return one follow-up task.

**What I checked against the 129 files**
- **Changed code files:** each of the changed non-test code files has at least one reader who read it in full or read its diff with the surrounding functions.
- **Files no reader named:** `daemon/network.rs`, `daemon/worker.rs`, `daemon/minimal.rs`, `node/sim/scenario.rs`, `node/sim/lifecycle_characterization.rs` and `node/local.rs`. I read their diffs: they box `SyncMessage` and add the new fields to fixtures and to `JoinRecord`, nothing else.
- **Adapted existing tests:** the Rust tests lost three assertion lines in all (two in `workspace_lifecycle.rs`, one in `context_views.rs`), each with assertions added in the same file. The site's `model.test.ts` and e2e spec were rewritten (8 and 11 assertion lines removed, 20 and 11 added); I did not read those two diffs.
- **Plan-named tests:** all present by name except the two already reported (`init_pins_the_lead_role_and_the_goals_completion_rule`, `a_goal_created_with_no_formation_follows_peer_review`). Refusal of role commands on a daemon that does not host the goal has its own test (`roles.rs:571`).
- **Exit-criteria greps:** `binding.roles`, quoted `coordinator`/`judge`, `administrator` and `--integrator` find nothing at 8c086c1.
- **Scripts:** none of the scripts that create a goal without a formation depends on an author's declaration, beyond the two already reported.

**Suspicions I chased that came to nothing**
- The new `.expect("other rule")` in `farm.rs` `requirement` is unreachable, because normalization dedups and collapses `Any` parts.
- The `head.unwrap()` and `anchor.unwrap()` calls added in `flow.rs`, `projection.rs` and `closure.rs` sit behind effectiveness checks.
- Enrolled agent names (32 bytes of a-z, 0-9, `-`) always pass `is_member_name`.
- `goal status` tolerates an unreadable formation.
- `stage_ready` checks standing before it resolves, so the `fold.rs:1103` ordering mistake has no sibling there.

**The gap**
`Verifier::resolve` now re-validates the whole formation once per (context, anchor) pair and deep-copies the role map on every hit. `desired_effects` scans the whole history once per uncounted result. The only performance workload uses a single anchor, is ignored and has no gate. One reader mentioned the first point and left it unmeasured.

**For the summary: the unmet exit criterion**
`check_t1.py --network local` and `simulate_machines/run.py --quick` did not pass on this commit; the owner waived them. I read the retained artifacts under `output/` and they support the builder's claim that the failure predates this phase:
- The same T1 local-mode step ("M2 and M3 exchange/decrypt notes without coordinator") timed out in three runs on 2026-10-04 on protocol-2 builds, for example `output/t1-local/20261004T122309Z-17abf0ef`.
- The only passing T1 run that day used default mode with relays.
- The machine simulation last passed under the `lan` profile on 2026-10-04 06:07 at c58bd30 (protocol 1).

So the breakage window opens two days before Phase 4. The artifacts do not say whether the cause is the Mac's network or an older code change.
